findings.description: The bucket has no ACL specified (defaults may allow public access) and is explicitly commented as public, exposing customer data (customer-master.xlsx) to unauthenticated access over the internet.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects stored in this bucket (including sensitive customer data) are not encrypted at rest.
Versioning is not enabled, meaning objects can be overwritten or deleted without recovery, increasing risk of data loss or tampering going undetected.
A sensitive file (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded to the aws_s3_bucket.data bucket, which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing customer master data to unauthorized access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket holding financial data, leaving stored objects unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so objects in the operations bucket are stored unencrypted.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so objects in the data-science bucket are stored unencrypted.
